# Perform McLeod-Li test

<small>Source: [`man/performMcLeodLiTest.Rd`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/man/performMcLeodLiTest.Rd) · Help: `?performMcLeodLiTest`</small>

Applies the Ljung-Box test to squared residuals.

## Usage

```r
performMcLeodLiTest(model, data = NULL, lags = 10)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   an object of class `lm`.

`data`
:   optional data frame the model was fitted to. When `NULL`, the default, the model frame of `model` is used. The statistic is computed from the residuals of `model`, so `data` does not change the result; it is accepted so that every test takes `(model, data, ...)`. Before 0.15.0 the second argument was `lags`: a number passed there by position is still read as `lags`, with a warning that shows the new call; that form stops working in 1.0.0.

`lags`
:   number of lags for the Ljung-Box test.

## Value

An object of class `htest` containing the test statistic, p-value and degrees of freedom.

## Details

Serial correlation in \(e_t^2\) indicates conditional heteroscedasticity. The Ljung-Box statistic is compared to a chi-square distribution with the chosen number of lags.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit. Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in
[`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported models*.

## References

McLeod, A. I., & Li, W. K. (1983). Diagnostic checking ARMA time series models using squared-residual autocorrelations. *Journal of Time Series Analysis*, 4(4), 269–273.

## Examples

```r
 data(mtcars)
 m <- lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
 performMcLeodLiTest(m, lags = 10)
```
